skill.name: software-testing-router
skill.description: Choose testing interfaces for CLI, API, web, Qt, and desktop applications, with scoped automation helpers and evidence-based acceptance checks.
skill.summary: Route software tests to suitable interfaces and verify observable results without relying on repeated screenshot-driven actions.
skill.author: hunxuankai

security_audit.summary: All 152 static findings are false positives involving documented commands, scoped automation, local evidence files, research URLs, and multilingual text. No evidence found of credential theft, data exfiltration, malicious obfuscation, or prompt injection. Desktop actions can modify the selected application; macOS native behavior remains unverified on actual hardware.

content.value_statement: Choosing the wrong testing interface can increase effort and leave acceptance requirements unverified. This skill selects suitable interfaces and checks observable outcomes with scoped desktop helpers.
actual_capabilities: Select CLI, API, DOM, UIA, AX, Qt, or visual checks according to the behavior that needs verification.
Inspect Windows application controls and run scoped set, invoke, and wait actions using Python and PowerShell.
Provide a macOS Accessibility runner with exact selectors, target identity checks, and permission checks, without requesting additional system privileges.
Record desktop progress in durable journals and distinguish completed steps from actions with unknown outcomes after timeouts.
Guide browser tests using real clicks, scoped locators, response checks, and independently verified output artifacts.
Define Qt signal, cancellation, and visual comparison checks while separating internal tests from packaged application acceptance.
limitations: Native macOS behavior has not been verified on actual Intel or Apple Silicon hardware; Linux has no bundled native GUI driver.
Windows UIA requires Python 3.10+, PowerShell 7, an interactive desktop, and controls exposing the required automation patterns.
The installed package excludes development tests, fixtures, browsers, and third-party testing dependencies.
Only set, invoke, and wait desktop actions are provided; keyboard shortcuts, drag operations, and universal speed improvements are not established.

use_cases.title: Validate a Packaged Windows Export
use_cases.description: Inspect an EXE, fill its form, invoke export, and independently verify fresh output without requiring application source.
use_cases.target_user: QA engineers testing packaged Windows applications

use_cases.title: Check Browser Submission Behavior
use_cases.description: Verify that a real button click produces the expected request, business response, interface state, and output artifact.

use_cases.title: Separate Qt and Delivery Checks
use_cases.description: Plan signal and cancellation tests separately from packaged application and visual acceptance checks.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Starting Interface
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [application] and [acceptance requirement]. Identify available testing interfaces, recommend a minimal first check, and state what remains unverified.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: choose a testing route before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Windows Application
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect [Windows EXE] using its observed PID and executable path. Report windows, supported UIA patterns, unique selectors, and blockers without changing application state.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: establish a safe desktop test scope.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a Browser Export
prompt_templates.prompt: Test [URL] using real form interaction and [expected output]. Correlate the click with its response, verify business results, and inspect fresh output.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: verify an end-to-end browser workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Handle Interrupted Desktop Actions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [desktop workflow], [journal], and current output artifacts. Distinguish completed steps from unknown actions, avoid automatic replay, and propose targeted verification.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: recover evidence after an interrupted desktop test.

output_examples.input: Choose a route to verify a Windows EXE exports the entered name and quantity.
output: Route: inspect the verified process with UIA and identify unique form controls.
Checks: fill the form, invoke export once, wait for completion, and independently read a newly generated output file.
Boundary: a returned button invocation alone does not prove export success.

output_examples.input: Assess a browser export that returns HTTP 200 but reports a failed business operation.
output: Result: fail the business assertion despite the successful HTTP status.
Evidence: preserve the click-correlated response, visible failure state, and absence of a fresh successful export.
Boundary: do not replace the button interaction with a direct API call.

output_examples.input: Plan native testing for a macOS application when Accessibility permission is missing.
output: Status: blocked by missing Accessibility permission; no native action verified.
Next step: request user assistance under the current session rules, then recheck permission and target identity.
Boundary: the helper does not modify TCC settings, and native macOS compatibility remains unverified on actual hardware.

best_practices: Select the smallest testing interface that can prove the acceptance requirement, and document its verification boundary.
Confirm target identity and unique control scope before actions; use condition waits and a bounded worker deadline.
Use fresh output directories or task identifiers, verify actual artifact contents, and inspect journals before recovering interrupted actions.
anti_patterns: Treating API success, a returned button invocation, or an existing file as proof of a complete user workflow.
Hiding ambiguous selectors with the first match, guessing coordinates, or automatically replaying actions after a timeout.
Claiming unsupported platform coverage, counting skipped tests as passed, or promising an unmeasured speed improvement.

faq.question: Does this skill require application source code?
faq.answer: Windows UIA can inspect suitable packaged applications without source. Qt internal tests require source and a compatible project environment.

faq.question: Which systems have execution evidence?
faq.answer: The package records Windows 10 examples. Native macOS, Windows 11, and Linux execution are not established by those results.

faq.question: Does it install testing dependencies automatically?
faq.answer: The runtime package does not include development dependencies. Use existing project tools and obtain authorization for any required installation.

faq.question: Can it change Accessibility permissions or elevate privileges?
faq.answer: No. The macOS helper checks existing permission without prompting or modifying TCC, and the workflow does not authorize elevation.

faq.question: What happens when a desktop action times out?
faq.answer: The worker stops, while the target application remains running. Review the journal and actual state because a started action may have completed.

faq.question: Does it replace screenshots and visual acceptance?
faq.answer: No. Layout, clipping, colors, and rendering require controlled visual evidence; successful API or accessibility checks cannot prove appearance.
